work_item: (e) Point Role Planning reproducibility (N=10, Household Ledger/topic, no Focus Module, no Writer call)
topic: 冷蔵庫のクリスパードロワー(野菜室)には低湿度・高湿度の2種類があり、正しく使い分けると食品が長持ちする。高湿度は葉物野菜がしおれるのを防ぎ、低湿度は果物が放出するエチレンガスを逃がして周囲の食品が早く傷むのを防ぐ。(Iowa State University Extension and Outreach等の情報に基づく)

results.point_one_role: Reframe the crisper as a tool for managing interactions among foods, not simply as a fruit-versus-vegetable sorter. It should show that the practical benefit of the low-humidity setting is partly protecting nearby produce from ethylene exposure.
results.point_two_role: Add a boundary-setting decision that comes before choosing a humidity setting: some foods should not be assigned to either crisper drawer. This makes the advice more useful than treating the two settings as a universal storage solution.

results.point_one_role: Use the Ledger’s mechanism to replace the misleading “fruit versus vegetable” shortcut with a practical sorting test: match low humidity to ethylene-producing foods and high humidity to foods that lose water and wilt quickly.
results.point_two_role: Show where the crisper rule stops applying by separating foods that should bypass the drawer from foods whose household setting is genuinely unsettled.

results.point_one_role: Reframe the crisper as a tool for managing interactions among foods, not merely as a bin assigned to one item. Its practical value is that venting ethylene from foods such as apples or pears can also protect nearby produce from ripening too quickly.
results.point_two_role: Set a practical boundary for the drawer advice by showing that humidity selection is not always the first storage decision. Before choosing low or high humidity, listeners should determine whether the food belongs in the refrigerator at all.

results.point_one_role: Make the memorable insight about food-to-food interaction: an ethylene-producing item can speed up the spoilage of nearby produce, so the drawer choice affects the whole mixed load, not just one item.
results.point_two_role: Set a practical boundary around the crisper rule by showing that choosing a humidity setting comes only after deciding whether the food belongs in the refrigerator at all.

results.point_one_role: Reframe the crisper as a shared environment: the setting affects not only the food inside the drawer, but also how ethylene-producing items affect nearby produce.
results.point_two_role: Give the listener a practical boundary for applying the rule by showing why commercial humidity numbers and broad food categories cannot automatically determine a household drawer setting.

results.point_one_role: Reframe the crisper slider as a control for two physical problems—airflow and water loss—rather than as a simple fruit-versus-vegetable label. Turn that distinction into a practical sorting rule: use ventilation for foods that release substantial ethylene, and moisture retention for foods that wilt quickly.
results.point_two_role: Provide the practical boundary of the crisper system by showing that not every produce item should be assigned to one of its two settings. Use the verified storage locations for tomatoes, bananas, potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, and garlic to prevent listeners from applying the drawer rule too broadly.

results.point_one_role: Make the central mechanism operational by reframing the crisper as a shared-air management tool, not simply a fruit-or-vegetable bin. It should show how the choice protects either neighboring food from ethylene exposure or a vulnerable item from rapid water loss.
results.point_two_role: Add a practical third branch to the storage decision: recognize when neither crisper setting is the right destination, and show how to respond when household guidance for a specific item is inconsistent.

results.point_one_role: Turn the humidity science into a practical sorting method: classify produce by behavior—an ethylene source or a moisture-loss victim—rather than by the fruit-versus-vegetable label.
results.point_two_role: Draw the practical boundary around the crisper advice: before choosing a humidity setting, decide whether the food belongs in a refrigerator at all.

results.point_one_role: Make the central mechanism operational by teaching listeners to diagnose the drawer from what the food is doing, rather than memorizing a fruit-versus-vegetable list.
results.point_two_role: Set a practical boundary around the crisper advice by introducing a two-stage decision: first decide whether the food belongs in the refrigerator at all, then choose a humidity setting.

results.point_one_role: A practical boundary-setting twist: show that some produce should bypass the crisper-drawer system altogether, rather than simply being assigned to low or high humidity.
results.point_two_role: An evidence-based decision boundary: explain why commercial humidity numbers and household crisper settings cannot be treated as interchangeable, especially for produce with conflicting household guidance.
